# Torque budget — DAST-1, 2026-09-09

*Generated by [mechlint](https://github.com/amirhpd/mechlint) `torque` from
`src/description/urdf/description.urdf.xacro` and `mechlint.yaml`. Regenerate with the command
at the bottom rather than editing the numbers here.*

> **Outdated (2026-11-11).** These numbers are for the old 5-servo links (`rotary`, `arm_1..3`,
> `gripper_3`). The arm has since been redesigned (`base_2`, `link_1..link_5`, `tip`) and
> `mechlint.yaml` remapped to it. Regenerate before relying on any figure below.

## The question

Does an MG996R hold each joint of the 6-DOF arm, empty and with 100 g / 200 g in the gripper?

## The answer

**No.** Joints 2, 3 and 4 are over budget, and joint 2 is over budget *before it picks anything
up*: 1.053 N·m of arm against 1.079 N·m of stall torque, at 6 V, with no margin at all.

| Joint | Servo | Stall @ 6 V | empty | 100 g | 200 g |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joint_1 | MG996R | 1.079 N·m | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| joint_2 | MG996R | 1.079 N·m | **1.053** | **1.651** | **2.249** |
| joint_3 | MG996R | 1.079 N·m | 0.519 | **0.965** | **1.411** |
| joint_4 | MG996R | 1.079 N·m | 0.112 | 0.369 | **0.626** |
| joint_5 | MG996R | 1.079 N·m | 0.011 | 0.180 | 0.350 |
| joint_6 | none yet | — | 0.011 | 0.183 | 0.354 |

Worst-case |torque| in N·m over 2048 sampled poses, including every corner of the joint-limit
box. **Bold** is a fail at safety factor 2.0. joint_1 turns about the mounting axis, so gravity
applies no torque about it at any pose — that zero is real, and it means joint_1 is sized by
friction and acceleration, which mechlint does not model.

Worst pose for joint_2 at 200 g (rad): `joint_1 -1.223  joint_2 +1.509  joint_3 +0.150
joint_4 +0.010  joint_5 +0.745  joint_6 -0.015` — the arm out and up, as expected.

## No servo in the database fixes it

Every entry, driving all six joints, judged at 200 g and safety factor 2.0:

| Servo | At | Stall | Mass | joint_2 margin | Still fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MG996R | 6 V | 1.079 N·m | 55 g | 0.24× | 2, 3, 4 |
| XC330-M288-T | 5 V | 0.930 N·m | 23 g | 0.21× | 2, 3, 4 |
| XL430-W250-T | 11.1 V | 1.400 N·m | 57 g | 0.31× | 2, 3 |
| 2XL430-W250-T | 11.1 V | 1.400 N·m | 98 g | 0.31× | 2, 3 |
| NEMA 17 + 5.18:1 | 1.68 A | 2.000 N·m | 520 g | 0.44× | 2, 3 |
| DS3218MG | 6.8 V | 2.108 N·m | 60 g | 0.47× | 2, 3 |
| DS3225MG | 6.8 V | 2.403 N·m | 60 g | 0.53× | 2, 3 |

joint_2 needs **4.50 N·m** to pass at 200 g with a 2× factor. The strongest 60 g servo in the
database gives 2.40. So this is not a motor-selection problem: **the arm is too long and too
heavy for any servo of this class**, and the fix is geometry — shorter links, mass moved
inboard, a lighter forearm, or a geared/counterbalanced shoulder — not a bigger DS-series servo.

A DS3225 at 6.8 V does clear the *raw* 2.249 N·m at 200 g (margin 1.07× on stall with no safety
factor). That is a stall figure from a reseller table, on a joint that also has to accelerate.
Building to it would mean running the shoulder at its stall limit, continuously, on trust.

## What these numbers are, and are not

- **Static.** Gravity holding, nothing accelerating. A real move needs more. That is what the
  safety factor is for, and 2.0 is a convention, not physics.
- **Stall torque, `low` confidence.** The MG996R figure is 11 kgf·cm from
  [servodatabase](https://servodatabase.com/servo/towerpro/mg996r) — a clone-market datasheet.
  Measured samples come in lower, and nothing published says what it holds continuously.
- **Masses are estimates,** from the STLs at PLA 1.24 g/cm³ and 30 % infill, plus 55 g per servo
  from the actuator database and the 30 g gripper motor from `mechlint.yaml`. Only `base_link`
  (210 g) and the Kinect (500 g) were weighed.
- **`arm_1.stl` and `base.stl` are not watertight** (M001), so their masses come from a convex
  hull — an over-estimate. arm_1 is downstream of joint_2, so the shoulder number is pessimistic
  by whatever that hull adds.
- **The Kinect is not in any of this.** It is eye-to-hand, on a stick beside the robot, so no
  joint carries it. mechlint works that out from the chain: every joint between it and the world
  is fixed.
- **Servo swaps above change only what a joint is judged against,** not what is bolted to the
  links — `components:` in `mechlint.yaml` still says MG996R. A heavier servo would make the
  arm heavier too, so those margins are slightly optimistic.

## Related findings

`mechlint check` also reports **U007** on joints 1–5: every joint declares `effort="20.0"` N·m
against a servo that delivers 1.079. A controller clamping at twenty times what the motor can do
is not clamping.

## Reproduce

```bash
mechlint torque -P 0 -P 100 -P 200      # this table
mechlint check                          # plus units, tensors, masses, meshes
mechlint actuators --min-torque 4.5     # what would hold joint_2. Nothing does.
```
